doc.title: Carol Bash interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2012

title: Music in the film and music clearance
summary: All film music is composed, performed or arranged by Williams; clearance needs a music supervisor and a budget estimate.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: What about the — was all the music in the film Mary Lou’s music?
Or, well some of it was stuff that she had arranged perhaps.

Yes, exactly. What I intend to do is, the music in the film is either going to be music that she composed, performed or arranged. So one of those three things. She touched it on one of those levels. Yeah, that’s the intent. That all the music you hear is somehow credited to her on some level.
And do you have assistance with that? In fact I think we had talked about your music clearance person that you had worked with. That’s a whole other ballgame too.

That’s a whole other ballgame. You’re getting right into the gut here, Monk, with your questions. Yeah music clearance is just a whole other ball of wax. Because it’s tracking down the copyright owners and the publishers of all these music compositions and that is so difficult a task at times, that you almost need to have somebody on board that really knows this stuff. So it just behooves me to hire a music supervisor, someone who really understands the music legalities and contracting and negotiating and all that. There’s no way I would ever want to do that or have my associate or my co-producer do that. It’s just too time-consuming and you just need someone that really has that expertise.

And are you able to — at what point do you put that in your funding applications? How do you — you know what I mean — because you don’t necessarily know what music you’re going to use from the get-go.

Um hum. Well what I would do is initially, I mean I always had a music supervisor in mind, someone who has a really good history of working with other filmmakers who I admire. And actually, excuse me, this woman, Rina Kosersky, my music supervisor, was a huge fan of Mary Lou Williams, although she ended up not being my music supervisor. She’s now working with a foundation. What I did was make a phone call to her and say “how much money should I put in the budget for music?” So basically it might not be the © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-
most accurate figure but it’s based on her knowledge and her expertise and so that figure goes into the budget.
No it’s not. No, no. Don’t say that about those rocket scientists. They really are rocket scientists. I am not.
